indicators.note: a new development of the letters means they are worked into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poisoning alarm breaks out as the latest twist in a news story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new development' rearranges SCARE plus IN; 'Poison' at the front is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known toxic element, the classic poisoner's choice in detective fiction.

parts.note: the two words 'The' and 'A' are each examples of the grammatical word class asked for, so the question asks what both of them are

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'The A?' as a grammar question: 'the' is the definite one of these and 'a' the indefinite one.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'the' and 'a' are the definite and indefinite determiners of this name.

clue.text: Foreign coppers assume disagreement to increase resistance

indicators.note: to assume something is to take it on, so the coin word takes the quarrel word into itself

parts.note: the sen is a small coin of Japan and other Asian countries, a foreign copper
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: Police officers abroad get into a row and dig their heels in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police, but here it means small coins from abroad; 'assume' (take on) signals the coin word taking in the quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To make rigid or firmer is to build up resistance to bending or pressure.

indicators.note: grotesque means distorted out of shape, so the next word's letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Some ghastly creature lurking in the gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grotesque' rearranges THING. 'Dark' is a noun here, as in 'after dark'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness between dusk and dawn; 'after dark' means after sunset.

clue.text: Transport to the crest for the shoot

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle for carrying goods
a ridge is the crest of a hill or roof

explanation.surface: Hauling gear up to the hilltop ready for a day's shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' simply joins CART to RIDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A shell loaded into a gun is what a shooting party fires.

clue.text: The bounder going into action falls

indicators.note: one piece going into another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: a case is a legal action brought in court
a cad or bounder is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A rotter springs into action and takes a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls' looks like a verb, but it is the noun, a waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a small waterfall, water tumbling over rocks in steps.

indicators.note: doubly says the word that follows is to be taken twice in a row

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A very solid start before having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply places the second piece after the doubled firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot chocolate-flavoured beverage made from roasted cacao powder.

clue.text: Material for building craft housing with style

indicators.note: housing means containing, so the ships wrap round the joining word

parts.note: SS stands for steamships, craft plural
and means with, joining two things
tone can mean the character or style of something

explanation.surface: Building boats that are fitted out stylishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' is plural here, two ships; 'housing' signals the ships wrapping round 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedimentary rock long quarried and cut into blocks for walls.

clue.text: A people backing one could be a bloomer

indicators.note: backing here means going backwards, so the word for people is read in reverse

parts.note: men means people, persons
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crowd supporting someone might be making a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns MEN into NEM. 'A bloomer' suggests a blunder, but here it is something that blooms, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering plant is something that blooms, so it is a bloomer in a literal sense.

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose, a reason for acting
less can mean without, as in 'a year less a day'

explanation.surface: Someone carrying on non-stop without any good cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives 'without' first, but the charade is built in answer order: END then LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbroken, continuing with no stop or pause, goes on forever.

parts.note: describes the small lever a finger squeezes to fire a gun, rather than an employee pushed to be sacked

explanation.walkthrough: 'discharge' hints at sacking someone, but the thing pressed is part of a gun, and pressing it makes the gun discharge.
explanation.definitionFit: The lever on a firearm that is squeezed to fire the weapon.

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
to minister to someone is to tend them, look after them

explanation.surface: Making a claim against a government minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' looks like a noun, a politician; it is the verb, to look after.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert or maintain a point in argument is to claim it is true.

clue.text: Where people may eat tea, if care is taken

indicators.note: letters that are taken apart and reassembled form a new word, so these are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice on drinking your tea carefully at a café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is taken' rearranges the nine letters of TEA, IF and CARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service restaurant where diners queue and carry their own meals to tables.

parts.note: read not as 'deeply asleep' but as the noise a sleeper makes while breathing heavily

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound asleep' usually means deeply asleep; read 'sound' as a noun: the noise a sleeper makes.
explanation.definitionFit: The rasping noise of heavy breathing through the nose and mouth during sleep.

clue.text: Bondsman turning in before being seen out

indicators.note: the word for before is seen on the outside, wrapping round the other piece

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: turning means the little word in is read backwards

explanation.surface: A bail guarantor going inside before being let out again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes NI, which ERE holds, since ERE is 'being seen out'. 'Bondsman' is not a bail guarantor: ERNIE is the computer that draws the winning numbers for UK Premium Bonds, a state-run savings lottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's random number machine picks the prize winners among Premium Bond holders.

clue.text: Running away from work in principle

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: an element can be a basic principle, as in the elements of a subject
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Shirking a job in theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Running off secretly to marry, typically without parental consent.

indicators.note: one piece is about the other when it surrounds it

parts.note: discs are gramophone records
over means finished, done

explanation.surface: Learning that the record books are closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the records surrounding 'finished'; 'the records' is plural, so its word ends in S.
explanation.definitionFit: To come upon or learn something for the first time is to find it.

indicators.note: the letters are taken back to raw material and remade into a new word

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe giving no letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that something stems from race is a damning one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in origin' rearranges ITS and RACIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking or sharply disparaging comment ridicules its target, so it is critical.

parts.note: not applying cosmetics or inventing stories, but forming part of a whole, as constituent parts do

explanation.walkthrough: 'Making up' hints at cosmetics or lying; read it as constituting, forming part of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituent part is one of the pieces that together form a whole.

indicators.note: after places the green word behind the study word

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
vert is the heraldic term for green

explanation.surface: Becoming environmentally minded after some research.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' suggests eco-friendly, but it is VERT, the heraldry colour. 'Turn' means change into something else.
explanation.definitionFit: To change something into another form is to turn it, as lead into gold.

clue.text: The mace used as a weapon

indicators.note: used means put to work or reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ceremonial club taken up as a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' rearranges THE and MACE; 'as a' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad heavy blade used for cutting through vegetation or as a weapon.

clue.text: Some wines (terrible ones!) contain such a compound

indicators.note: Some here means a portion of the following words, the letters running across them unbroken

explanation.surface: Bad wines are full of nasty chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' marks the answer as part of 'wineS TERrible'; 'ones' and 'contain' only serve the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An organic chemical made from an acid and an alcohol, giving wines and fruits their aromas.

clue.text: Marked right-about right-and so was misleading

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the marked word goes round the letter

parts.note: a correct answer is ticked when marked right

explanation.surface: A marker who gives ticks for wrong answers is fooling everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside TICKED; 'and so' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceived or fooled someone, past tense of a verb meaning to deceive.

indicators.note: roundabout says the word reads the same coming round from either end

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A fairground ride, read on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roundabout' says the answer reads the same both ways. The clue runs on into 23-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that turns or spins things is a device for rotation.

indicators.note: about means around, so the strict word goes round the letter

parts.note: nice can mean precise or strict, as in a nice distinction

indicators.note: end of the word month means its last letter

explanation.surface: A stern rule about holidays at the end of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' in its old sense of exact or fine is easy to miss. 'month-end' gives H, put inside NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a shallow recess in a wall, such as for a statue.

clue.text: The thief, it's clear, isn't reformable

indicators.note: able to be reformed, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe giving no letter

explanation.surface: A judge declares that a thief can't be reformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformable' rearranges CLEAR and ISNT; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who commits theft, the legal term for stealing property.

parts.note: la is French for the
the in English

explanation.surface: Completing the preceding clue: a turning device, named in two languages.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is in 21-down: 'device for' turning, carried here by the dots. 'the bilingual' is the word 'the' in French then English.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine tool that spins wood or metal while it is shaped is a device for turning.

clue.text: Heather may be put in charge in time

indicators.note: may be put, followed by 'in time', says the charge abbreviation is placed within the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Heather may be promoted to the boss role eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths, the low shrubs of moorland.

clue.text: High spot for a woman-an opportunity to relax

parts.note: Eve is a woman's name, the first woman in Genesis
a rest is a break in which to relax

explanation.surface: A woman finds a high spot ideal for taking it easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's tallest mountain is the ultimate high point on Earth.

definitions.meaning: a bat-and-ball sport played by two teams of eleven
a small chirping insect related to the grasshopper

explanation.walkthrough: A bat-and-ball game popular in Britain and the Commonwealth, and a small insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name covers an English bat-and-ball sport and a chirping insect.

parts.note: not a backer of company directors but a physical frame holding up a tabletop

explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter of the board' suggests someone backing the directors; it is a stand holding up a tabletop.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of legs and a crossbar that holds up a table top.

clue.text: Hero's love for thin retiring leftist

parts.note: lean means thin

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for a leftist is read backwards

parts.note: a red is a left-winger

explanation.surface: Someone's sweetheart picked for being a slender, shy socialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns RED into DER. In Greek myth Hero was the priestess whose lover swam the Hellespont nightly to see her.
explanation.definitionFit: In the myth, the young man who swam to meet the priestess Hero and drowned.
